About Tim Clarke:A versatile and expressive musician, Buffalo, NY-based trumpet/cornet/flugelhorn player Tim Clarke performs and records with a wide array of creative, jazz-oriented groups throughout Western New York and it's surrounding areas. A creditable performer of modern styles of improvisational music, Tim is a noted practitioner of √Ç¬ìChicago-styleï traditional jazz, having developed a love for this music which goes back to the Chicago recordings of Louis Armstrong in the 1920s. In 2020, Tim was recipient of JazzBuffalo's √Ç¬ìJohn Hunt Jazz Musician of the Yearï. A native of Eugene Oregon, Tim received his BA and MA from the University of Oregon School of Music and Dance in 1993. Tim's fruitful relationship with the Oregon Festival of American Music goes back 25 years, first as a charter member of the Emerald City Jazz Kings, and later as a featured guest soloist.
About Andy Weinzler:Andy Weinzler has performed with many world renowned jazz and popular artists, having toured with the big band of trumpeter Maynard Ferguson and performed with the big bands of Tommy Dorsey, Glenn Miller, John LaBarbera, Lionel Hampton with Kevin Mahogany. He has also been invited to tour with Chuck Mangione and the big bands of Woody Herman and Buddy Rich.In 1990 Andy joined Gap Mangione's New Big Band as a tenor and soprano saxophone soloist. He has performed on three of Gap's CDs featuring world-class musicians Steve Gadd, Tony Levin, John Patitucci and fellow saxophonists Pat LaBarbera and Gerry Niewood. Gap's New Big Band and Quintet have performed regularly at the Xerox Rochester International Jazz Festival and in 2015 Gap released the quintet recording 'Live in Toronto' featuring Andy and Pat LaBarbera.Other artists Andy has performed with include Dizzy Gillespie, Doc Severinsen, Tony Bennett, Aretha Franklin, Johnny Mathis, Natalie Cole, Maureen McGovern, Michael Feinstein, Frankie Valli, the Temptations, Spinners and many more. Performances with the Buffalo Philharmonic Orchestra (BPO) began when he was just 17 years old and he can be heard on two BPO recordings (Naxos): 'Gershwin: Rhapsody in Blue' and 'Duke Ellington: Black, Brown & Beige'. Recently he has also been featured as jazz tenor saxophone soloist with the Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO). Andy has performed for many Broadway shows including òWest Side Story', òChorus Line' and ò42nd Street' and he was featured in a 2013 Issue of òSaxophone Journal' (Dorn Publications).Andy received his Bachelor of Music degree in Saxophone Performance from the prestigious Eastman School of Music, and a Master of Music degree in Jazz Studies from the University of Miami. He was Assistant Professor of Jazz Studies at St. Francis Xavier University, Antigonish, Nova Scotia, Canada, from 1986 to 1989 where he was a member of the faculty jazz sextet, JazFX, which performed at major western-Canada jazz festivals and recorded for the CBC and Mark Records.

Throughout the class, our farm bunnies are free to move about the space as they chooseïthey may visit your mat, nibble treats, or hop and flop nearby.After yoga, you'll be invited to hand-feed the bunnies and spend a few quiet minutes connecting with them in their bunny room.This listing is cross-posted on our website at www.bluedotacres.ca/events
Yoga with Bunnies is different from goat yoga or puppy yoga.
Bunnies are prey animals, which means they connect in softer, quieter ways. When a bunny chooses to hop by your mat, flop nearby, or even nibble a leafy green we've placed for them, it's a gentle giftïnot something we can (or want to) force. If a bunny decides to approach you during class, it's a special moment.This makes bunny yoga calmer, more mindful, and often more introspective than other animal yoga experiences. The best way to √Ç¬ìmake a bunny friendï is by focusing on your own yoga practice. Loud or unpredictable movements will cause the bunnies to retreat, while stillness and presence invite them closer.For this reason, bunny yoga is best suited for adults and young people who are genuinely interested in yoga and able to enjoy the mindfulness aspect of the practice.
Quick Comparison√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêá Bunny YogaAtmosphere: Calm, serene, and restorativeInteraction: Subtleïbunnies may hop, flop, or curiously nibble nearbyFocus: Your yoga practice comes first; bunnies enhance mindfulnessEnergy Level: Quiet and peaceful, ideal for unwinding√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêê Goat YogaAtmosphere: Playful and livelyInteraction: Goats climb, nudge, and get into mischiefFocus: More about fun with the animals than traditional yogaEnergy Level: High-spirited, social, and entertaining√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üê∂ Puppy YogaAtmosphere: Heartwarming and affectionateInteraction: Puppies jump, lick, and tumble aroundFocus: Playful bonding with puppies alongside light yogaEnergy Level: Vibrant, joyful, and interactiveIn summary:
If you're seeking calm, quiet, and a deeper yoga practice with the possibility of gentle bunny interactions, this is the experience for you. If you're looking for lively antics and playful chaos, goat or puppy yoga might be a better fit.
Our Bunny-Led, Consent-Based ApproachAt Blue Dot Acres, respect for animals is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that meaningful connections happen when animals are free to make their own choices. That's why bunny yoga looks very different from goat or puppy yogaïit's not about picking up or snuggling bunnies, but about inviting them to join us on their own terms.When you arrive, you'll set up your mat in our open, airy space. Once class begins, the bunny room door is openedïthis is their invitation. Some bunnies may hop over, nibble, or flop nearby; others may choose to stay in their safe space. Both choices are respected.Why does this matter? Bunnies are prey animalsïsensitive, cautious, and deeply aware of their surroundings. When they decide to approach you during yoga, it's not because they were placed in your lap or coaxedïit's because they feel safe. That choice is powerful. It helps children and adults alike understand that real trust is built, not taken. In many ways, it mirrors the lessons of yoga itself: patience, presence, and respect for boundaries.During class, simply stay with your practice. If a bunny comes to you, enjoy the moment quietlyïsome like gentle pats while eating, while others prefer space. A bunny flopping beside you is a sign of deep comfort, a gift we never take for granted. At the end of class, we'll gather any leftover greens so you can hand-feed the bunnies if they wish.This approach ensures that the experience stays calm, respectful, and enjoyable for everyoneïhumans and bunnies alike. For us, this class is more than just an event. It's a way of teaching consent, mindfulness, and care in a world that often overlooks the quieter voices.

Name: Relaxation Yoga with Bunnies
Description:
Find your calmïsoft stretches, deep breaths, and a few furry-eared visitorsBreathe deeply, stretch softly, and let the bunnies set the pace. In this relaxation yoga class, our floppy-eared friends may hop by or flop nearby as you sink into stillness. Afterward, you'll be invited to meet them more closely and discover a little about their everyday care.Tickets are $30 per person and includes;a 60 minute relaxation yoga sessionconnection time with the bunnies with a peak at the bunny room, hand feeding opportunities, and a chance to learn about these sweet creaturessomething from the produce stand to take home*Bring your own yoga mat or ask to borrow one of ours!What to ExpectYoga with Bunnies takes place on our farm in our heated, open-concept workshop. Classes are guided by a rotating yoga instructor, alternating weekly between Tova from Reframe Family Yoga and Alicja from @mindfulspacesbyala.Participants will enjoy a gentle yoga class focused on choice, self-acceptance, and listening to your body. Throughout the class, our farm bunnies are free to move about the space as they chooseïthey may visit your mat, nibble treats, or hop and flop nearby.After yoga, you'll be invited to hand-feed the bunnies and spend a few quiet minutes connecting with them in their bunny room.This listing is cross-posted on our website at www.bluedotacres.ca/events
Yoga with Bunnies is different from goat yoga or puppy yoga.
Bunnies are prey animals, which means they connect in softer, quieter ways. When a bunny chooses to hop by your mat, flop nearby, or even nibble a leafy green we've placed for them, it's a gentle giftïnot something we can (or want to) force. If a bunny decides to approach you during class, it's a special moment.This makes bunny yoga calmer, more mindful, and often more introspective than other animal yoga experiences. The best way to √Ç¬ìmake a bunny friendï is by focusing on your own yoga practice. Loud or unpredictable movements will cause the bunnies to retreat, while stillness and presence invite them closer.For this reason, bunny yoga is best suited for adults and young people who are genuinely interested in yoga and able to enjoy the mindfulness aspect of the practice.
Quick Comparison√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêá Bunny YogaAtmosphere: Calm, serene, and restorativeInteraction: Subtleïbunnies may hop, flop, or curiously nibble nearbyFocus: Your yoga practice comes first; bunnies enhance mindfulnessEnergy Level: Quiet and peaceful, ideal for unwinding√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêê Goat YogaAtmosphere: Playful and livelyInteraction: Goats climb, nudge, and get into mischiefFocus: More about fun with the animals than traditional yogaEnergy Level: High-spirited, social, and entertaining√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üê∂ Puppy YogaAtmosphere: Heartwarming and affectionateInteraction: Puppies jump, lick, and tumble aroundFocus: Playful bonding with puppies alongside light yogaEnergy Level: Vibrant, joyful, and interactiveIn summary:
If you're seeking calm, quiet, and a deeper yoga practice with the possibility of gentle bunny interactions, this is the experience for you. If you're looking for lively antics and playful chaos, goat or puppy yoga might be a better fit.
Our Bunny-Led, Consent-Based ApproachAt Blue Dot Acres, respect for animals is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that meaningful connections happen when animals are free to make their own choices. That's why bunny yoga looks very different from goat or puppy yogaïit's not about picking up or snuggling bunnies, but about inviting them to join us on their own terms.When you arrive, you'll set up your mat in our open, airy space. Once class begins, the bunny room door is openedïthis is their invitation. Some bunnies may hop over, nibble, or flop nearby; others may choose to stay in their safe space. Both choices are respected.Why does this matter? Bunnies are prey animalsïsensitive, cautious, and deeply aware of their surroundings. When they decide to approach you during yoga, it's not because they were placed in your lap or coaxedïit's because they feel safe. That choice is powerful. It helps children and adults alike understand that real trust is built, not taken. In many ways, it mirrors the lessons of yoga itself: patience, presence, and respect for boundaries.During class, simply stay with your practice. If a bunny comes to you, enjoy the moment quietlyïsome like gentle pats while eating, while others prefer space. A bunny flopping beside you is a sign of deep comfort, a gift we never take for granted. At the end of class, we'll gather any leftover greens so you can hand-feed the bunnies if they wish.This approach ensures that the experience stays calm, respectful, and enjoyable for everyoneïhumans and bunnies alike. For us, this class is more than just an event. It's a way of teaching consent, mindfulness, and care in a world that often overlooks the quieter voices.
If this date doesn't work for you, additional Bunny Yoga dates are listed on our website under events. Sign up to be on our email list to find out about our monthly offerings!www.bluedotacres.ca

Name: Geeky Book Club: February Meeting - The Blacktongue Thief
Organizer: Chelsea & Dave: Geeky Book Club Hosts
Description:
Join us to discuss The Blacktongue Thief by Christopher BuehlmanWelcome to Geeky Book Club!
Who are we? We are a group of "geeky" readers who meet monthly to discuss fantasy and sci-fi novels.What are the meetings like? Our meetings are focused on discussing this month's novel. If you've ever been frustrated after attending a book club where no-one actually talked about the book (or even finished it!) geeky book club may be for you! Questions will be provided to help guide the discussion, and we encourage you to share your own thoughts and takeways with the group.What kind of books do we read? We generally alternate between fantasy and sci-fi novels each month. Our books are chosen by vote; once you've attended your first meeting you will receive links to vote on our future books..This month we are reading Christopher Buehlman's 2021 fantasy novel, The Blacktongue Thief.Kinch Na Shannack owes the Takers Guild a small fortune for his education as a thief, which includes (but is not limited to) lock-picking, knife-fighting, wall-scaling, fall-breaking, lie-weaving, trap-making, plus a few small magics. His debt has driven him to lie in wait by the old forest road, planning to rob the next traveler that crosses his path.

But today, Kinch Na Shannack has picked the wrong mark.

Galva is a knight, a survivor of the brutal goblin wars, and handmaiden of the goddess of death. She is searching for her queen, missing since a distant northern city fell to giants.

Unsuccessful in his robbery and lucky to escape with his life, Kinch now finds his fate entangled with Galva's. Common enemies and uncommon dangers force thief and knight on an epic journey where goblins hunger for human flesh, krakens hunt in dark waters, and honor is a luxury few can afford..Welcome, new members, to geeky book club! Whether you're a lifelong lover of reading, picking it back up after a break, or just getting into it, we are happy to have you join us! We meet monthly to discuss fantasy and sci-fi books, and occasionally for other social events in-between.Please keep the following in mind:Space is limited; if you are no longer able to attend please cancel your booking so that someone else can attend in your place.The library is attached to a community centre. We are meeting in the program room inside the library, not a community centre room.We love a good debate, but please remember to keep it respectful and on-topic. Everyone is welcome at geeky book club and discrimination of any kind will not be tolerated.If you have any questions or concerns, please use the link to contact us at the bottom of this page. Geeky book club is hosted by an independant group, not the library, so the library staff may not be able to answer your book-club-specific questions.
Address: Burlington Public Library - Tansley Woods Branch1996 Itabashi WayBurlington, ON L7M 4J8 Canada

The concert will also be the premiere of Sonny-Ray Day Rider's work that is the CLC's ISCM Commissioning Project for Indigenous Artists.Wesley Shen is a Toronto-based pianist and harpsichordist specializing in the performance of contemporary music. He can be found in equal measure as a solo, collaborative, chamber and orchestral musician. He regularly performs with a number of groups including Continuum New Music, New Music Concerts, Esprit Orchestra, Soundstreams, and FAWN Chamber Creative. He is also a core member of the Freesound Ensemble, one of Toronto's newer contemporary music collectives. He has also received numerous grants from the Canada Council of the Arts to commission over a dozen new works for both solo harpsichord and solo piano. He continues to strive to create and contribute to these deeply fruitful collaborative relationships between performers and composers, as well as promote the harpsichord as an expressive and exciting contemporary music instrument.As well as the piano and harpsichord, Wesley has added a number of additional instruments to his palette, namely the sh√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬Öç and more recently the Ondes Martenot. Her work focuses on rediscovering music and musicians obscured by time and social constrictions, as well as challenging the conventions of classical violin through contemporary repertoire.Roan received her BM and MM degrees in violin performance from the Manhattan School of Music, graduating from her Masters with the Hugo Kortschak Commencement Award for Outstanding Achievement in Chamber Music. Name: FAMILY DAY LOVE THEMED Family Yoga with Bunnies
Description:
Feel the love in this warm & fuzzy relaxation yoga class with soft stretches, deep breaths, and bunny visitors.Slow down and share some warm and fuzzy, love-filled moments. Breathe deeply, stretch softly, and let our floppy-eared friends set the pace as they wander or rest nearby. Afterward, enjoy time with the bunnies, learn about their care, and make your own hot chocolate to take with you.Tickets are $25 per person and includes;a 45-60 minute relaxation yoga session (depending on what the kids can handle!)connection time with the bunnies with a peak at the bunny room, hand feeding opportunities, and a chance to learn about these sweet creatureshot chocolate and flower to take the love home with you!*Bring your own yoga mat or ask to borrow one of ours!What to ExpectYoga with Bunnies takes place on our farm in our heated, open-concept workshop with a cozy atmosphere. This gentle morning class will include connection-based poses, designed at a pace for children 4-10 years.The class will be led by Ange @angefromtheheart and will focus on playful connection, self-acceptance, and listening to your body. Throughout the practice, our farm bunnies are free to move about the space as they chooseïthey may visit your mat, nibble treats, or hop and flop nearby.After yoga, you'll be invited to hand-feed the bunnies and spend a few quiet minutes connecting with them in their bunny room. As a sweet touch, each participant will also make a cup of hot chocolate to take home, along with a flower.This listing is cross-posted on our website at www.bluedotacres.ca/events
Yoga with Bunnies is different from goat yoga or puppy yoga.
Bunnies are prey animals, which means they connect in softer, quieter ways. When a bunny chooses to hop by your mat, flop nearby, or even nibble a leafy green we've placed for them, it's a gentle giftïnot something we can (or want to) force. If a bunny decides to approach you during class, it's a special moment.This makes bunny yoga calmer, more mindful, and often more introspective than other animal yoga experiences. The best way to √Ç¬ìmake a bunny friendï is by focusing on your own yoga practice. Loud or unpredictable movements will cause the bunnies to retreat, while stillness and presence invite them closer.For this reason, bunny yoga is best suited for adults and young people who are genuinely interested in yoga and able to enjoy the mindfulness aspect of the practice.
Quick Comparison√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêá Bunny YogaAtmosphere: Calm, serene, and restorativeInteraction: Subtleïbunnies may hop, flop, or curiously nibble nearbyFocus: Your yoga practice comes first; bunnies enhance mindfulnessEnergy Level: Quiet and peaceful, ideal for unwinding√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêê Goat YogaAtmosphere: Playful and livelyInteraction: Goats climb, nudge, and get into mischiefFocus: More about fun with the animals than traditional yogaEnergy Level: High-spirited, social, and entertaining√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üê∂ Puppy YogaAtmosphere: Heartwarming and affectionateInteraction: Puppies jump, lick, and tumble aroundFocus: Playful bonding with puppies alongside light yogaEnergy Level: Vibrant, joyful, and interactiveIn summary:
If you're seeking calm, quiet, and a deeper yoga practice with the possibility of gentle bunny interactions, this is the experience for you. If you're looking for lively antics and playful chaos, goat or puppy yoga might be a better fit.
Our Bunny-Led, Consent-Based ApproachAt Blue Dot Acres, respect for animals is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that meaningful connections happen when animals are free to make their own choices. That's why bunny yoga looks very different from goat or puppy yogaïit's not about picking up or snuggling bunnies, but about inviting them to join us on their own terms.When you arrive, you'll set up your mat in our open, airy space. Once class begins, the bunny room door is openedïthis is their invitation. Some bunnies may hop over, nibble, or flop nearby; others may choose to stay in their safe space. Both choices are respected.Why does this matter? Bunnies are prey animalsïsensitive, cautious, and deeply aware of their surroundings. When they decide to approach you during yoga, it's not because they were placed in your lap or coaxedïit's because they feel safe. That choice is powerful. It helps children and adults alike understand that real trust is built, not taken. In many ways, it mirrors the lessons of yoga itself: patience, presence, and respect for boundaries.During class, simply stay with your practice. If a bunny comes to you, enjoy the moment quietlyïsome like gentle pats while eating, while others prefer space. A bunny flopping beside you is a sign of deep comfort, a gift we never take for granted. At the end of class, we'll gather any leftover greens so you can hand-feed the bunnies if they wish.This approach ensures that the experience stays calm, respectful, and enjoyable for everyoneïhumans and bunnies alike. For us, this class is more than just an event. It's a way of teaching consent, mindfulness, and care in a world that often overlooks the quieter voices.
If this date doesn't work for you, additional Bunny Yoga dates are listed on our website under events. Sign up to be on our email list to find out about our monthly offerings!www.bluedotacres.ca

We have been teaching him to put his front paws on your lap if he would like to politely ask for a treat.

Name: LOVE THEMED Relaxation Yoga with Bunnies
Description:
Feel the love in this warm & fuzzy relaxation yoga class with soft stretches, deep breaths, and bunny visitors.Slow down and share a warm, fuzzy Valentine moment. Breathe deeply, stretch softly, and let our floppy-eared friends set the pace as they wander or rest nearby. Afterward, enjoy time with the bunnies, learn about their care, and make your own hot chocolate to take with you.Tickets are $30 per person and includes;a 60 minute relaxation yoga sessionconnection time with the bunnies with a peak at the bunny room, hand feeding opportunities, and a chance to learn about these sweet creatureshot chocolate and flower to take the love home with you!*Bring your own yoga mat or ask to borrow one of ours!What to ExpectYoga with Bunnies takes place on our farm in our heated, open-concept workshop, softly lit with candlelight for a cozy Valentine's atmosphere. This gentle afternoon class will include optional partner and connection-based poses, designed to be shared with a partner, friend, family member, or someone you love.The class will be led by Diana from Shivana Yoga and will focus on choice, self-acceptance, and listening to your body. Throughout the practice, our farm bunnies are free to move about the space as they chooseïthey may visit your mat, nibble treats, or hop and flop nearby.After yoga, you'll be invited to hand-feed the bunnies and spend a few quiet minutes connecting with them in their bunny room. As a sweet Valentine touch, each participant will also make a cup of hot chocolate to take home, along with a flower.This listing is cross-posted on our website at www.bluedotacres.ca/events
Yoga with Bunnies is different from goat yoga or puppy yoga.
Bunnies are prey animals, which means they connect in softer, quieter ways. When a bunny chooses to hop by your mat, flop nearby, or even nibble a leafy green we've placed for them, it's a gentle giftïnot something we can (or want to) force. If a bunny decides to approach you during class, it's a special moment.This makes bunny yoga calmer, more mindful, and often more introspective than other animal yoga experiences. The best way to √Ç¬ìmake a bunny friendï is by focusing on your own yoga practice. Loud or unpredictable movements will cause the bunnies to retreat, while stillness and presence invite them closer.For this reason, bunny yoga is best suited for adults and young people who are genuinely interested in yoga and able to enjoy the mindfulness aspect of the practice.
Quick Comparison√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêá Bunny YogaAtmosphere: Calm, serene, and restorativeInteraction: Subtleïbunnies may hop, flop, or curiously nibble nearbyFocus: Your yoga practice comes first; bunnies enhance mindfulnessEnergy Level: Quiet and peaceful, ideal for unwinding√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üêê Goat YogaAtmosphere: Playful and livelyInteraction: Goats climb, nudge, and get into mischiefFocus: More about fun with the animals than traditional yogaEnergy Level: High-spirited, social, and entertaining√É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç√Ç¬∞üê∂ Puppy YogaAtmosphere: Heartwarming and affectionateInteraction: Puppies jump, lick, and tumble aroundFocus: Playful bonding with puppies alongside light yogaEnergy Level: Vibrant, joyful, and interactiveIn summary:
If you're seeking calm, quiet, and a deeper yoga practice with the possibility of gentle bunny interactions, this is the experience for you. If you're looking for lively antics and playful chaos, goat or puppy yoga might be a better fit.
Our Bunny-Led, Consent-Based ApproachAt Blue Dot Acres, respect for animals is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that meaningful connections happen when animals are free to make their own choices. That's why bunny yoga looks very different from goat or puppy yogaïit's not about picking up or snuggling bunnies, but about inviting them to join us on their own terms.When you arrive, you'll set up your mat in our open, airy space. Once class begins, the bunny room door is openedïthis is their invitation. Some bunnies may hop over, nibble, or flop nearby; others may choose to stay in their safe space. Both choices are respected.Why does this matter? Bunnies are prey animalsïsensitive, cautious, and deeply aware of their surroundings. When they decide to approach you during yoga, it's not because they were placed in your lap or coaxedïit's because they feel safe. That choice is powerful. It helps children and adults alike understand that real trust is built, not taken. In many ways, it mirrors the lessons of yoga itself: patience, presence, and respect for boundaries.During class, simply stay with your practice. If a bunny comes to you, enjoy the moment quietlyïsome like gentle pats while eating, while others prefer space. A bunny flopping beside you is a sign of deep comfort, a gift we never take for granted. At the end of class, we'll gather any leftover greens so you can hand-feed the bunnies if they wish.This approach ensures that the experience stays calm, respectful, and enjoyable for everyoneïhumans and bunnies alike. For us, this class is more than just an event. It's a way of teaching consent, mindfulness, and care in a world that often overlooks the quieter voices.
If this date doesn't work for you, additional Bunny Yoga dates are listed on our website under events. Sign up to be on our email list to find out about our monthly offerings!www.bluedotacres.ca

Yoga with Bunnies is different from goat yoga or puppy yoga.
Bunnies are prey animals, which means they connect in softer, quieter ways. When a bunny chooses to hop by your mat, flop nearby, or even nibble a leafy green we've placed for them, it's a gentle giftïnot something we can (or want to) force. If a bunny decides to approach you during class, it's a special moment.This makes bunny yoga calmer, more mindful, and often more introspective than other animal yoga experiences. If you're seeking calm, quiet, and a deeper yoga practice with the possibility of gentle bunny interactions, this is the experience for you. If you're looking for lively antics and playful chaos, goat or puppy yoga might be a better fit.
Our Bunny-Led, Consent-Based ApproachAt Blue Dot Acres, respect for animals is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that meaningful connections happen when animals are free to make their own choices. That's why bunny yoga looks very different from goat or puppy yogaïit's not about picking up or snuggling bunnies, but about inviting them to join us on their own terms.When you arrive, you'll set up your mat in our open, airy space. Once class begins, the bunny room door is openedïthis is their invitation. Some bunnies may hop over, nibble, or flop nearby; others may choose to stay in their safe space. When they decide to approach you during yoga, it's not because they were placed in your lap or coaxedïit's because they feel safe. That choice is powerful. It helps children and adults alike understand that real trust is built, not taken. In many ways, it mirrors the lessons of yoga itself: patience, presence, and respect for boundaries.During class, simply stay with your practice. If a bunny comes to you, enjoy the moment quietlyïsome like gentle pats while eating, while others prefer space. A bunny flopping beside you is a sign of deep comfort, a gift we never take for granted. At the end of class, we'll gather any leftover greens so you can hand-feed the bunnies if they wish.This approach ensures that the experience stays calm, respectful, and enjoyable for everyoneïhumans and bunnies alike. For us, this class is more than just an event. It's a way of teaching consent, mindfulness, and care in a world that often overlooks the quieter voices.

Konrad Eisenbichler is a prize-winning scholar whose research focuses on the intersection of literature, politics, and religion in Renaissance Italy, with additional work on the literature and history of Italian immigration in Canada. Professor Eisenbichler has held several senior academic roles, including President of the Sixteenth Century Society and Conference, the Canadian Society for Renaissance Studies, and the Canadian Society for Italian Studies. Description:
Please call  1-833-240-0310 if you have questions or to request additional times if event shows sold out.The pottery wheel for couples offers a captivating and immersive experience for two individuals looking to explore the art of pottery and create unique curves and designs together. This specialized wheel workshop is designed to accommodate two participants, allowing them to engage in a shared creative journey.
Crafted with precision and durability, the pottery wheel provides a sturdy foundation for the couple to work on. Its smooth rotating surface responds to the gentle touch of their hands, encouraging a seamless interaction with the clay. The wheel's speed can be easily adjusted, catering to the preferences and skill levels of both individuals.
As the couple sits together or side by side, they are greeted by an array of high-quality clay, ready to be transformed into works of art. The couple's hands meet the malleable material, guiding it onto the spinning wheel. They begin to shape and mold the clay, discovering the sensual curves and lines that emerge under their fingertips.
The wheel allows for synchronized movements, as the couple's hands work in harmony, sharing the weight and pressure applied to the clay. They communicate, exchanging ideas and inspiration, as they explore various techniques and experiment with different pottery forms. Together, they embrace the beauty of imperfection, celebrating the uniqueness of each curve and design that emerges from their collaboration.
With skilled guidance or through their own intuition, the couple can create an assortment of pottery pieces, ranging from delicate vases to intricate bowls or even sculptural artworks. The wheel's versatile design allows them to incorporate their personal flair, adding decorative elements, textured patterns, or intricate carvings to their creations.
Throughout the pottery wheel experience, the couple becomes immersed in a world of creativity and self-expression. They discover the joy of working with their hands, feeling the clay come alive beneath their touch. The process becomes a metaphor for their relationship, as they learn to navigate the ebb and flow of collaboration, supporting and inspiring one another along the way.
In the end, the couple emerges with a collection of pottery pieces that serve as tangible reminders of their shared experience. Each creation tells a story of their journey, encapsulating their unique connection and the artistic exploration they embarked upon together. Whether they display their pottery in their home or gift them to loved ones, these handcrafted pieces become cherished symbols of their bond and the memories they created through their shared passion for pottery.O ptional- pieces can be painted and kiln fired once dry.

Name: Valentine's Make-a-Mug on a Pottery wheel for couples -Bay/Dundas Toronto
Description:
Please call  1-833-240-0310 if you have questions or to request additional times if event shows sold out.Welcome to the captivating world of pottery! In this hands-on class, you will embark on a creative journey to make your own unique mug on a pottery wheel. Guided by experienced instructor, you will learn the art of wheel throwing and experience the joy of transforming a lump of clay into a functional masterpiece.

The class begins with an introduction to the pottery wheel and its various components. You'll become acquainted with the tools and materials used throughout the process, including different types of clay, glazes, and sculpting tools. The instructor will share their expertise, providing valuable insights and tips to help you achieve the best results.

Once you have a solid understanding of the pottery wheel, it's time to get your hands dirty! You'll be given a block of clay and shown how to properly center and prepare it on the wheel. As you start spinning the wheel, you'll feel the clay respond to your touch, gradually taking shape beneath your fingertips.

Under the guidance of the instructor, you will learn essential techniques such as pulling, shaping, and thinning the clay walls to create the desired form of your mug. The process requires focus, patience, and a willingness to experiment. As you refine your skills, you'll gain confidence in controlling the clay's movement and shape.

Once you've molded the basic structure of your mug, it's time to add personal touches and details. You can get creative with handles, textures, and decorative elements to make your mug truly one-of-a-kind. The instructor will provide suggestions and support as you explore different design options, encouraging you to unleash your imagination.

After completing the shaping and decoration, your mug will need to dry and undergo the initial firing process. This ensures that it holds its form and is ready for glazing. Once the pieces are dry you'll have an option to book a subsequent session for $10, where you'll learn about glazes and different coloring techniques, allowing you to add vibrant or subtle hues to your creation.

Once the glazing is complete, your mug will be fired again in a kiln, bringing out the vibrant colors and transforming the raw clay into a durable, functional piece of art. Finally, it's time to behold your masterpiece and take it home with you, ready to be enjoyed with every sip of your favorite beverage.

Participating in a "Make Your Own Mug on Pottery Wheel" class not only provides a fantastic opportunity to explore your creativity but also offers a therapeutic experience that allows you to disconnect from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Whether you're a complete beginner or have some prior experience, this class promises to be an enriching and rewarding journey into the world of pottery. So roll up your sleeves, embrace the tactile nature of clay, and get ready to make a mug that will be treasured for years to come.

Description:
Come and enjoy the experience of tote painting. You will be guided step by step to learn how to paint on tote from start to finishThe paint on tote  class involves the application of paint on a cotton tote to create decorative or artistic designs. The class focuses on exploring different painting techniques and styles that can be used to enhance the natural beauty of the tote.
Here is a description of what the class may cover:
Introduction to Totes: The class begins with an introduction to totes as an art medium. Students learn about the characteristics of totes, such as the grain patterns, texture, and natural color variations, which can influence the painting process.
Preparation and Priming: Students are taught how to prepare the tote for painting. This may include applying a primer to improve paint adhesion and prevent bleeding.
Color Theory and Design: The class covers the fundamentals of color theory and design principles as they apply to painting on totes. Students learn about color mixing, shading, blending, and composition to create visually appealing artwork.
Painting Techniques: Various painting techniques specific to totes are explored. This may include brush techniques, stippling, dry brushing, glazing, and layering to achieve different effects and textures on the cotton.
Subject Matter and Themes: Students are encouraged to experiment with different subject matters and themes for their tote paintings. This may range from nature-inspired motifs like landscapes, flowers, and animals to abstract or contemporary designs.
Finishing and Sealing: Once the painting is complete, the class covers techniques for finishing and sealing the artwork to protect it and enhance its longevity. This may involve applying a varnish,  or sealant to preserve the paint and highlight the natural beauty of the tote.
Display and Presentation: The class concludes with discussions on how to display and present the finished totes. Students learn about framing options, mounting techniques, and ways to showcase their artwork in various settings.
Throughout the class, students receive guidance from the instructor, who provides demonstrations, critiques, and individualized feedback to help them improve their painting skills. The aim is to foster creativity and encourage students to explore the unique possibilities offered by painting on totes.

Name: Valentine's Day-Make-a-Mug on Pottery wheel for couples, Oakville Lakeshore
Description:
Please call  1-833-240-0310 if you have questions or to request additional times if event shows sold out.Welcome to the captivating world of pottery! In this hands-on class, you will embark on a creative journey to make your own unique mug on a pottery wheel. Guided by experienced instructor, you will learn the art of wheel throwing and experience the joy of transforming a lump of clay into a functional masterpiece.

The class begins with an introduction to the pottery wheel and its various components. You'll become acquainted with the tools and materials used throughout the process, including different types of clay, glazes, and sculpting tools. The instructor will share their expertise, providing valuable insights and tips to help you achieve the best results.

Once you have a solid understanding of the pottery wheel, it's time to get your hands dirty! You'll be given a block of clay and shown how to properly center and prepare it on the wheel. As you start spinning the wheel, you'll feel the clay respond to your touch, gradually taking shape beneath your fingertips.

Under the guidance of the instructor, you will learn essential techniques such as pulling, shaping, and thinning the clay walls to create the desired form of your mug. The process requires focus, patience, and a willingness to experiment. As you refine your skills, you'll gain confidence in controlling the clay's movement and shape.

Once you've molded the basic structure of your mug, it's time to add personal touches and details. You can get creative with handles, textures, and decorative elements to make your mug truly one-of-a-kind. The instructor will provide suggestions and support as you explore different design options, encouraging you to unleash your imagination.

After completing the shaping and decoration, your mug will need to dry and undergo the initial firing process. This ensures that it holds its form and is ready for glazing. Once the pieces are dry you'll have an option to book a subsequent session for $10, where you'll learn about glazes and different coloring techniques, allowing you to add vibrant or subtle hues to your creation.

Once the glazing is complete, your mug will be fired again in a kiln, bringing out the vibrant colors and transforming the raw clay into a durable, functional piece of art. Finally, it's time to behold your masterpiece and take it home with you, ready to be enjoyed with every sip of your favorite beverage.

Participating in a "Make Your Own Mug on Pottery Wheel" class not only provides a fantastic opportunity to explore your creativity but also offers a therapeutic experience that allows you to disconnect from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Whether you're a complete beginner or have some prior experience, this class promises to be an enriching and rewarding journey into the world of pottery. So roll up your sleeves, embrace the tactile nature of clay, and get ready to make a mug that will be treasured for years to come.

With some minor accommodations those on the autism spectrum can provide a competitive edge in the workplace, but only if there is an accurate diagnosis, training and accommodations. Girls are less likely to display their autism symptoms compared to boys and therefore diagnosis can be delayed. This can have severe consequences leading to a heavier caregiver burden. After cooking, enjoy a warm sit-down meal or pack it up to take home.

Founded by flutist Carmen Maret and guitarist Andrew Bergeron, the duo has developed a singular artistic voice through two decades of collaboration, live performance, and original composition.Based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Folias Duo has independently booked and performed over 700 concerts across the U.S., South America, and Europe. Their performances span a wide range of venuesïfrom chamber music series and libraries to art galleries, house concerts, and guitar societies. During the pandemic, they produced 40 livestream broadcasts, continuing their creative output when many ensembles paused.Their discography includes eight albums, with the most recentïHeartdanceïdescribed by Fanfare Magazine as "a life-enhancing experience." Earlier recordings, produced by Latin Grammy-nominated Sergei Kvitko for Blue Griffin Records, were followed by three albums on their own Folias Music label, recorded at Sono Luminus Studios with Grammy-winning engineer Daniel Shores and producer Dan Merceruio.Maret and Bergeron have composed and recorded over 70 original works for flute and guitarïmore than any duo of their kind worldwide. Their instrumentation includes C flute, alto flute, bass flute, piccolo, and tambin, paired with nylon-string guitar, creating a richly expressive and distinctive sound palette. They have also collaborated with string quartets, orchestras, and folk ensembles. Bergeron's broader works include a symphony, a guitar concerto, and a forthcoming flute concerto premiering in November 2025.As dedicated educators, they co-direct the Folias Music School and serve on the faculty at Aquinas College and Grand Rapids Community College. Maret recently completed a one-year appointment at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music. She holds a Bachelor of Music from the University of MissouriïKansas City Conservatory and a Master of Music from Michigan State University. Bergeron holds a Bachelor of Arts from Grand Valley State University and a Master of Music from Michigan State University.Folias Duo's artistry is deeply tied to their way of life. Name: Group Event / Party up to 40 ppl / Canvas Painting Lakeshore/Bronte
Description: Up to 40 participants. Please call  716-244-2074 if you have questions or to request additional times if event shows sold out.Imagine stepping into a warmly lit studio, the air filled with the faint scent of acrylic paints and fresh canvases. Laughter echoes softly as friends, colleagues, or family members gather around long tables draped in protective plastic sheets, each person claiming their spot - a blank canvas, and a palette of vibrant colors. This is the essence of a group canvas painting eventïa communal celebration of artistry, where novices and seasoned painters alike come together to unleash their inner creativity under the guidance of an enthusiastic instructor. This event, often hosted as corporate team-building activities, transform ordinary evenings into memorable adventures in self-expression and collaboration.At its core, a group canvas painting event is designed to be accessible and fun, stripping away the intimidation often associated with fine art. Participants don't need prior experience; in fact, the beauty lies in the inclusivity. The session typically begins with a warm welcome from the host / instructor. They'll outline the evening's themeïperhaps a serene landscape like a sunset over rolling hills, a whimsical abstract design inspired by nature, or a seasonal motif such as blooming cherry blossoms in spring or cozy autumn leaves. Themes can be customized too: for a birthday party, it might be a personalized portrait of the guest of honor; for a corporate retreat, a motivational scene symbolizing teamwork, like interlocking gears forming a heart.As the group settles in, the instructor demonstrates the basics step by step. They'll start with sketching faint outlines on the canvas using light pencil marks or pre-printed guides for those who prefer structure. "First, we'll mix our base colors," the instructor might say, holding up a brush dipped in cerulean blue and cadmium yellow to create a lush green for foliage. Participants follow along, their brushes dipping into paint pots arranged neatly on shared traysïprimaries like red, blue, and yellow, alongside earthy tones, metallics for flair, and plenty of white for blending. The room buzzes with energy as people experiment: one might accidentally splatter paint, turning a mistake into a "happy accident" √É¬É√Ç¬É√É¬Ç la Bob Ross, while another meticulously layers shades for depth.What sets a group canvas painting event apart from solitary painting is the social dynamic. It's not just about the artwork; it's about the connections forged through shared laughter and encouragement. Strangers become friends as they peek at each other's canvases, offering compliments like, "I love how you added those golden highlights to the sun!" or tips such as, "Try thinning the paint with a bit of water for a watercolor effect." For couples on a date night, it becomes a romantic escapade, painting side by side and perhaps collaborating on a diptychïtwo canvases that form one complete image when placed together. Families use it as bonding time, with kids giggling over exaggerated features in a family portrait, while parents appreciate the mess-free setup (all supplies provided, no cleanup required at home).The event's structure ensures a relaxed pace, usually spanning one, or two   hours. Some events incorporate games, like "paint roulette" or musical charis where participants swap canvases mid-way, adding an element of surprise and hilarity as they adapt to someone else's style.Beyond the fun, these events offer tangible benefits. Creatively, they boost confidence; many leave amazed at their own abilities, clutching a framed-worthy piece to hang at home. Psychologically, painting in a group setting promotes mindfulness, reducing stress as brushes glide across canvas, focusing minds on the present. For teams, it's an excellent team-builder, fostering communication and problem-solvingïdeciding how to blend colors or compose elements mirrors workplace collaboration. Studies from art therapy research even suggest such activities enhance emotional well-being, releasing endorphins similar to those from exercise.As the session winds down, the instructor circles the room, providing final tips on blending edges or adding highlights. Participants step back to admire their work, often posing for group photos with their masterpieces held high.In today's fast-paced world, a group canvas painting event stands as a refreshing antidote to digital overloadïa hands-on, analog experience that reconnects people with their creative sides and each other. Whether it's a bachelorette party bursting with vibrant florals, a holiday gathering painting winter wonderlands, or a quiet friends' night recreating famous artworks with a twist, these events create lasting memories and tangible souvenirs. If you're seeking a way to spark joy, build bonds, or simply try something new, stepping into one of these colorful gatherings promises an evening painted in hues of happiness and discovery.

The instructor demonstrates various throwing techniques and encourages students to experiment with different shapes and forms. The focus is on developing skills such as pulling up walls, shaping vessels, and creating textures or patterns on the clay surface.Throughout the class, participants receive individual attention and guidance from the instructor, who offers tips and suggestions to improve their technique and troubleshoot any challenges they encounter. Name: Governance Model for scaled QA Automation.
Description:
Join us as we dive into the world of governance models for QA automation, exploring strategies for success and scalability.Governance Model for Scaled QA AutomationAs organizations expand their digital platforms and accelerate delivery, QA automation often scales faster than the processes designed to support it. What begins as a high-impact initiative can quickly turn into a complex ecosystem of scripts, tools, and frameworks that are difficult to govern, maintain, and evolve. Without a clear governance model, teams face duplicated effort, unstable automation, rising maintenance costs, and diminishing returns.This in-person session is designed to help QA leaders, Quality Engineers, automation architects, and delivery teams understand how to build and sustain a governance model that supports QA automation at scale. The focus is on creating structure without slowing teams down, enabling innovation while maintaining consistency, and ensuring automation remains reliable as organizations grow.During this session, we will explore how successful enterprises define ownership, establish standards, select and manage tools, and implement operational controls that allow automation programs to scale confidently across multiple teams and portfolios.
